utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Before we resume, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, the registry has made a complaint, which I think is justified, at the direction which you had put in your order and which I signed, making the Victims and Witnesses Section responsible for serving that witness summons, and they pointed out to me that they have previously said to the Prosecution it should never be the Victims and Witnesses Section. The point, which I agree with, is that the Victims and Witness Section has a particular function to perform. According to the Rules, it recommends protective measures and it looks after the witnesses when they arrive here, and they arrange their travel here. It would compromise the Section if they were also put into some sort of enforcement role. So I've directed the registry to ignore that part of the order, and I'll make it formal later, and somebody else from the registry will be responsible. But would you please make it clear to the people upstairs that they should never, ever suggest in an order that it should be the Victims and Witnesses Section to serve such things as summonses and subpoenas.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Sorry for this mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's all right. We've got it sorted out. Yes, Mr. Vasic. You were cross-examining. Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, before my colleague Vasic proceeds, I thought I should inform you that the accused has got back his glasses, that he can follow now the proceedings normally and regularly, and I should like to thank you for the attention. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you for letting us know. We're very grateful to hear that. Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Vasic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Yesterday we talked about isolation cells and you pointed at them for us. I'd like to ask you now: Who did you hear from about these isolation cells?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it from those people who were kept there, from inmates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From inmates who told you that they had been taken there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You testified yesterday that some persons were taken away and that they are missing to this day. I shall now ask you about each one of them individually who had you talked about -- who did you talk about. Who told you that Mr. Husein Dzano is gone and missing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to his neighbours in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Emir Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to his wife and his mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Cedic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About Mr. Cedic, I heard from his neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about Mr. Nurko Nisic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About Mr. Nurko Nisic, I heard it from his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husko Rikalo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About Husko Rikalo, I heard it from his mother, whom I saw in Sarajevo daily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramo Dzendusic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ramo Dzendusic, from his relatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that ten to 15 people were taken from Josanica and that nobody ever saw them again. Who did you discuss these people with?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked with their neighbours who were in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you did not give us the names of all the people.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know all those names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please, for your safety, because your voice is protected, will you please wait for me to switch off the microphone so that your voice doesn't get through my microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is also a problem with the translators, sir, so that pause is very important. If the microphone of the counsel who's asking you questions is left on, then your voice is no longer distorted, so for your own protection, you must have that pause.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you talked to neighbours and relatives, and when was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I talked to -- with them between 1996 -- ever since 1996, for the past three, four years. I found those people in Sarajevo. I met them, and they all said the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you testified about the group which went to pick plums, you mentioned Mr. Kasim Musanovic and Mr. Halim Konjo. Did you also mention them in your statements to OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I'm not sure. I believe I did, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These persons are not mentioned on page 7 of your first statement. This statement mentions eight persons, and neither Mr. Halim Konjo or Mr. Musanovic are among them.

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose I simply did not remember them at the time when I was giving the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, oh, you remembered about them afterwards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, just in relation to that last question, I think my friend mentioned that the witness didn't mention the names in his first statement. In the statement, the English version, 189A, on the 8th of November, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just wait a minute. Just to shortcut this, Mr. Vasic referred to page 7 of the first statement. Was he wrong about that, or was he wrong by overlooking the fact that the names are mentioned somewhere else in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think both. The first statement contains two pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's the one in November 1992. And in that first statement, he does mention --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: He does mention Musanovic. There's a slightly different spelling. And also in that first statement he does mention Halim Konjo, but under different circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the point is -- your point would be good for the first but not the second, I would have thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Vasic, these things should be put with some care. I understand you've got an awful lot of material that you've got to keep in mind, but do check before you make assertions. The witness doesn't have the document in front of him, and he can't check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in view of the objection, I should merely like to point out that I asked about the statement which was given to OTP investigators and page 7 of the statement. I did not ask anything about the statement which the witness gave to the Public Security Centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But your point, your point is only a good one if he hasn't mentioned it anywhere. The fact that he mentions it in one and not in another doesn't really carry any weight, if I may say so. Your point is that this is an afterthought, and it would be a good one, or it could be a good one, only if it had never been mentioned in these circumstances. So may I suggest you take the substance of the point and not this minute detail; it doesn't help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you testified about where and when you were exchanged, and you said there were about 30 other persons from the KP Dom. Could you give us the names of those persons who left with you for exchange and had been in the KP Dom with you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can. I can tell you as far as I can remember. There was Emir Mujezinovic, Alija Sljivo, Murid Islambasic, then Sead Dejovic. Other names I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you said that your wife was under house arrest, and since the time that you talked about she was in Foca and there were very many military and paramilitary formations on the streets. Wasn't it safer for her to be in the house in view of the situation in Foca at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer because he overlapped with the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't want to keep on saying this to you, but you must wait until there has been a pause after the question. In fact, your answer on that occasion actually overlapped the question itself. Now, please, we're all trying to understand the difficulties you are having, but you are not helping yourself and you're certainly not helping us if we lose the whole answer. We'll need the question asked again, I'm afraid, Mr. Vasic, so we get an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you think, in view of the situation in Foca, that it was safer for your wife to be in the house rather than on the street?

utterances.speaker: FWS-104 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That is also what the witness said the first time. And thank you, we have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Re-examination, Mr. Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, then, sir, your experience is over. Thank you for giving evidence. You may leave, but please wait until the blinds have been drawn so that you will be able to leave without the public seeing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, in relation to the next witness, there's a matter I'd like to raise in relation to protection measures. No protection measures have been granted. He has asked for image and a pseudonym, and perhaps that should be discussed in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Why? Is there some real problem about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No. Well, I suppose it's not essential in that sense. He didn't request protection measures when asked a while ago by the Prosecution. When he arrived at the Tribunal, he raised the matter. He states that he goes into -- he returns to Bosnia every year, and he's got a concern for his safety if his name is made known. And he returns to an area which is near the area of Foca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bakrac, I think we can probably assume that you will object to the protective measures sought, but that does fall within the usual parameters of granting them. Is there anything more you want to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, I have nothing to add. We stand by our earlier opinion, which you already know, and our objection is along those lines again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We look forward to hearing what you've got to say when you seek protective measures for one of your own witnesses. Yes, very well, then. Yes, Mr. Smith, we'll grant those protective measures. He already has a -- it's he, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He already has a pseudonym, 104.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That was the previous one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. 03.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: 03, yes. I believe a pseudonym sheet has been passed to the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not know if this is the convenient time, but to use the time before the witness arrives, regarding our submission for psychological expert witness and the response of the Prosecution. I trust that the response of the Prosecution has already reached you. We discussed it with members of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I have to say, Mr. Bakrac, it hasn't. There seems to have been some insoluble blockage in the passage from the registry floor to the Chambers floor, but I personally am having a great deal of difficulty in getting any documents. When was it filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 17th of January. That is the date on the document, 17th of January. I see we did not discuss it, and that is why I took the liberty of raising that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm grateful to you for having done so. Is there any possibility of us getting a copy so we can look at it perhaps during the morning adjournment?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will provide it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: As soon as we've got it, we'll raise it with you, Mr. Bakrac, so we've got it finalised. The witness pseudonym sheet will be Exhibit P417, and it is under seal. The second name on that list you don't provide any sort of a pseudonym for, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This person is not a witness in the case but it just refers to a relation of his which he'll be referring to a lot throughout his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So it will only be a reference to "my relation" or some such phrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So that we know that this second name on this sheet is that relation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. We might deal with the exit certificate, or whatever they call it, at the same time. Is there any objection to that being made an Exhibit, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that will be Exhibit P418. It too will be under seal, as will the English translation of it, which is P418A. Now, sir, will you please take the solemn declaration in the document which is being shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, sir. The transcript has got the witness's name. That should be now shown as FWS-3. We'll just pause to enable that to be done before it goes any further. Are you going to change the transcript now? Yes, you proceed, Mr. Smith. We still have to delete the name. You can't do that? Because the transcript now goes on the Internet, you see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be redacted, then. Proceed, Mr. Smith. Examined by Mr. Smith:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Court has granted you protection measures in this case in relation to your name and to your visual image. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In front of you is a piece of paper containing your name and date of birth at the top. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That paper is P417.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your testimony, if you need to refer to your uncle -- withdraw that. Does your uncle's name also appear on that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you need to refer to your uncle during your testimony, do not refer to his name, but just to the term "uncle."

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, in 1992, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I lived in Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live in the town of Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Not far from the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you live in an apartment building or a house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: In a house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you married at the time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any children?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you working?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnicity are you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, were you a member of the SDA political party in Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what level of involvement did you have in that party?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: As a supporter of the party only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you serving in a military unit before the war commenced?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. I was -- I served the Yugoslav People's Army, like all the other militarily-able men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you an active soldier before the war commenced in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what date did the war commence in Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: From what I can remember, it was the 7th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Why didn't you just lead -- I've told you so often just to lead on this issue. There is no issue left -- there could be no issue left as to the date upon which the war commenced in Foca. And if you had done what I've asked you, you wouldn't have got such an absurd answer. I can't resist saying that. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: An unexpected answer, but I take your point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the war commenced, where were you staying?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see when the war started? What could you personally see?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything. I only heard the shelling when it began and shots. I was at home. I didn't go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at one stage leave your house and go somewhere else to another place?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go from your house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: My wife and I went to my mother-in-law, and we stayed in her flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you leave your house that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Because we thought it was safer down there as the flat was in the town centre, and there were cellars. We were afraid of shells, and in our own house, there was no cellar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at your mother-in-law's flat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: A couple of days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that couple of days, did you see what was going on around, around her flat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No, because we never went anywhere, nor did we try to see what was going on around us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that couple of days, did you leave and go to someone else's house? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. We moved to the building where my uncle lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you move to your uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Because that cellar was overcrowded, there were too many people, and the conditions were poor. My wife was expecting, she was pregnant, and we had to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember what date -- did you -- what date did you leave for your uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at your uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, it could have been a week or two, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do whilst you were at, whilst you were at your uncle's house? Did you stay there, or did you move about the town?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No, I could not move about the town because it was too dangerous. We were in the house all the time; we never went out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during this time period, was the house searched?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how many times was it searched whilst you were at your uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Twice, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who searched the house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Members of the Serb army. I think they belonged to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they do when they searched the house, or what did they say?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: They were supposedly looking for weapons and, I don't know, they dug the entire house -- I don't know what they were really interested in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they find any weapons at the house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No, because we didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after being at your uncle's house for one or two weeks, where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Then I went back with my wife to my father's house where I used to live before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Because shelling had stopped and there was no danger from that score, so as far as our security was concerned, it was irrelevant whether we were in their house or in our house. We believed that it was better for us to be in our own house because this is where we used to live and this is where all of our things that we needed were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at your own house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Until 24th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the time that you were at your father's house, did you see what was happening around the town?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No, because we were not allowed to move about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who didn't allow you to move about the town?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It was publicly announced through a loudspeaker. There was a car that circled the town with a loudspeaker, and in that manner it was announced that Muslims were not allowed to move about the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it an official car or a private car?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It was a police vehicle, a Golf, blue and white.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the loudspeaker only pronounce that Muslims were not allowed to move around the town or Serbs as well?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It was only forbidden to the Muslims. This is what was announced through the loudspeaker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you stayed at the house till the 24th of May. What happened on the 24th of May that caused you to leave?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: A military policeman came on that day and took me into the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names of the military police that took you there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I don't remember their full names, but I know their nicknames and last names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were they?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: There was Drakul known as Zliko, Pikolo, a young guy named Dino known as Gira, one named Miletic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've mentioned four names. Was it just four people that took you to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe how you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, they knocked on the door. My wife came down, because we lived on the first floor, she opened the door, and they asked her whether there was anybody else in the house. She answered yes, me and my uncle were there, and they told her to have us come down. Later on, they simply looked at us, and they said they wouldn't touch us, and they left, but they also told us that we were not to move about, that we had to stay where we were. After a certain time, they came back again and they told us to get ready, that we were going for interrogation and that, after that, they would bring us back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who took you to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: These, these people. I left in one car, which was driven by Dino, and my uncle was taken in another car. They said that they needed to fetch another man as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dino the person you referred to as Gira earlier?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes, Dino known as Gira.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you the name of the other man they said they were going to fetch?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time did you arrive at the KP Dom on that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: In the evening hours, just before the dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was your uncle there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No, I was the first one to arrive. He came after me in another car, and with another man in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how long after you arrived did your uncle and this other man arrive?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Perhaps five or ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was this other man's name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Hajro Sabanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what work did he do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what work did he do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I am not sure exactly, but I know that he worked in the lumber factory, Maglic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you arrived at the KP Dom, did you see Halim Dedovic that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I saw him in the backyard of his house. Those same policemen, military policemen, took him from his house as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he taken before you were taken to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: They took him, but I didn't know where to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When your uncle and Hajro Sabanovic arrived at the KP Dom, were you inside the facility or out the front?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I was outside the compound. I was standing in front of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who brought Hajro and your uncle to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly who drove that car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once they arrived, what happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: The three of us went inside, into the compound in front of the administrative building, and we were told to wait.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you wait for?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Not very long, perhaps five or six minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was supervising you or looking after you on the outside of the KP Dom whilst you were waiting?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than your uncle and Hajro, who else was with you outside the KP Dom whilst you were waiting?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: We were waiting within the KP Dom. We were in the administrative building, in the hallway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you entered the administrative building, did you turn left or right as you go in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No. We waited there for five or six minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is inside the administrative building, just after the entrance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the lighting like inside, inside the KP Dom in this entrance area?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Visibility was quite low because it was becoming dark. There was no electricity, no light. And the guards that brought us in had flashlights, and this is what helped them move around the hallways of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say the guards that brought you in, who are you referring to? Is it the military police that brought you or is it someone else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Military police, but there were also a couple of guards who worked as guards in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were waiting in this entrance area in the administration building, did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard some screams and moans coming from one of the hallways of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the screams and moans -- where were they coming from? To the left of the entrance? To the hallway to the left or to the hallway to the right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It was a hallway to the left from the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise who these screams and moans were coming from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. The voice belonged to Halim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these screams and moans coming from the ground floor or another floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: They were coming from the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how long did this screaming and moaning last?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: A few minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whilst you were waiting in this area, did anything happen to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Zliko, Drakul, known as Zliko, threatened us. He was putting a knife under our chins, on our necks, and threatening with an automatic weapon. He harassed us while we were waiting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you specifically?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was saying he would shoot us, kill us. He didn't say anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from this Zliko who was there with you, was there anything else there at this entrance area?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. Some people were standing there, but since it was already dark, we couldn't really tell who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the screaming and the moaning ceased from Halim, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Then they came to fetch Hajro and took him along that same hallway from where the screams were coming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who took him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything after Hajro was taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. He started making screams, started moaning as well. That means that most likely they started beating him right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long this screaming and moaning lasted for?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Same thing; perhaps five minutes, a few minutes. I can't remember exactly, because I was in shock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after this, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: After that, they came to get me and told me that it was my turn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who came to get you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: One of those military policemen came. I can't remember which one it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say it was simply your turn or did he further explain what was going to happen to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No. He just said, "It's your turn. Let's go."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I was taken along the same hallway as Hajro, and we entered a room in that hallway which was on the left side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see when you arrived in the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I saw Hajro lying on the floor in blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he was lying on the floor in blood, where was the blood?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: On his clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who else was in the room other than Hajro?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Those military policemen who brought us in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Hajro say anything when you came into the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He couldn't say anything; he was unconscious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the other people in the room were the military police that brought you in. Can you restate the names of the people that were in that room of the military police?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: There was Zliko, Drakul; Miletic, Pikolo; Dino, known as Gira. And I think that was it, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to you when you were brought into the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, they put me next to the wall, facing the wall. I had to spread my arms and lean them against the wall, and then they also spread my legs as far apart as they could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they begin to question you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. They asked me whether I was an activist, a military activist of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you say to them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I replied that I was not an activist, that I was just a plain member of that party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ask you any other questions?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No. After that, they said, "Why are you lying?" and they started beating me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did they beat you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: They hit me on the back, around kidneys, in this area here, on my arms, with some kind of an object, but I couldn't tell which object, because it was dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many times were you hit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We should record where the witness was pointing to. It was at his back, about halfway down his back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many times were you hit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I can't remember how many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was in fact hitting you? You mentioned who was in the room, but do you know who was hitting you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I was hit first by Zliko, Drakul. And what happened later on I couldn't really tell because I was facing the wall, and also it was dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these hits cause you any pain?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were hit, was someone else brought into the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: When they stopped hitting me, they asked me again, "Why are you lying?" and said they were going to bring in somebody who would confirm that I was an activist in SDA. And then Halim showed up at the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about Halim when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. His face was swollen, bruised. He was all beaten up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Halim say anything when he came into the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: They asked him whether I was an SDA activist, and he replied that I was. And then they started hitting him again, because they asked him, "Well, why are you lying?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many times was he hit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I can't remember how many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they hitting him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: All over. All over his body. On his head, back, abdomen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst this was going on, was Hajro still on the floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Hajro was on the floor, but at that point some of them brought a bucket of water and splashed water on Hajro, and then he regained consciousness. Two of them helped him get up, and as he regained consciousness and started -- and was able to stand up, they started hitting him again. After a certain amount of time, due to these heavy blows, Hajro fell again and lost consciousness again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any conversation going on between Hajro and the people that were hitting him at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No, there was no conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who hit him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I can't remember which one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Hajro fell to the floor again, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Then Halim and I were taken out into the hallway and we remained waiting there. Later on, they brought in my uncle and took him inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see your uncle when you came out of the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I saw him as he was brought into the room because we were standing across from the door leading into that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your uncle was brought into the same room that you had just left?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear, hear anything in relation to your uncle from that room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: As he was entering the room, they said, "Don't --" one of them said, "Don't beat him. He's disabled." And then they started questioning him, but I didn't hear what he was asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were taken out of the room, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Halim and I were waiting there in the hallway in front of that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you wait for?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps five or ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Then they took out my uncle and Hajro out of that room and took them somewhere. Halim and I were taken back into the room. They locked up the door, and this is where we spent the rest of the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any beds in this room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No, there was just one chair there, and I sat in it the entire night while Halim lay on the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any physical injuries from your beating?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I was swollen and I had bruises from these heavy blows, but I couldn't see because there was no mirror; however, I did feel a strong pain in the areas where I was beaten from these heavy blows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did these pains last?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, it lasted a few days. It hurt until the bruises disappeared, perhaps seven to ten days. I can't remember exactly how long it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Halim have any visible injuries?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were they?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Facial injuries, from what I could see. His face was bloody, swollen. His eyes were so swollen that he could barely see. He also had lacerations on his face, scars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, the witness indicated the right side of his face with his hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Hajro have any visible injuries?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I couldn't see Hajro properly because it was dark. They only used their torches when they moved about, and it was only when I entered the room the first time and when I saw him on the floor, it was only then that I could see that his clothes were bloody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this incident relates to paragraph 5.23 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you slept -- or you stayed in the room in which you were beaten that night. The following day, were you taken somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. They took us to another building, to an isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which building was that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It was that building where other prisoners were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who took you there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: A guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you and Halim taken together?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes, they took us together and put us in the same room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen on the way to that, to that isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. As we came out of that administrative building, we were led away, not the one that was taking us but another guard called Burilo. We had to wait for him to open the door, a heavy metal door, and as we waited, he opened the door, passed behind us, and hit me twice here on the nape of my neck. The pain was severe. I did not expect that blow and was relaxed, so that it hurt badly. And afterwards when we reached the isolation cell and I spoke to Halim about that, and he told me that he had been hit too, but I never noticed that. He only told me when we -- after we reached the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what Burilo was wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was in that KP Dom uniform, I mean that guard uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was he when he hit you? Was he in front of you, to the side, or behind?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was behind me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where this other guard was that was escorting you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was also behind us, but he waited, was standing to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you, anything to you when he hit you, before or after?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No, he did not say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there appear to be any reason for you to be struck that way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: There was no reason. I do not know why he hit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this incident is referred to in Schedule A, number 3, and Schedule A, number 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in the isolation cell, was anyone else in there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. There were two other men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what ethnicity they were?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for what length of time did you spend in the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I stayed there until the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was one bed in the cell; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Correct. There was only one bed because the isolation cell had been in usage for one person only, and we were four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the four of you stay overnight in that cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I assume that the three of you slept on the floor.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken to after spending the night in the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: The next day, they moved me to a room with other prisoners where there was a large, a rather large group of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the number of that room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I think it was 16. It was on the ground floor to the left from the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the prisoners' building on the left-hand side or the prisoners' building on the right-hand side as you look at the KP Dom from the front?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: That entrance was to the right. There was one to the left and there was one on the right-hand side, and I was -- I went through the right one as you look from the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that Exhibit P88 be shown to the witness, please. It's the sketch of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any significance that you are the only one who uses this document, Mr. Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Possibly, Your Honour. I've always liked it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We don't.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It was this door here, and the isolation cells were here, and I was in these rooms here on the ground floor of this building. So the first entrance and then to the left, that's where the dormitory was where they took me that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can we agree that that is Room 16?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Agreed, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, we don't need the sketch any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in the room, about how many people -- the Room 16, how many people were in it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I'd say some 60 or 70 in that room because there were four dormitories in that room and a large anteroom, a hall, which connected those dormitories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whilst you were in that room, did you see anyone that had suffered from some injuries?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: At that time, that is, when I got there, nobody had any injuries, at least, I did not see anyone with any injuries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that room, Room 16? How many nights did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, I was brought there on the 24th. On the 25th, I was moved there, and I left on the 7th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the time --

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No. Sorry. Sorry. I was brought on the 24th; on the 25th I was transferred to the isolation cell; and on the 26th I was transferred to Room 16, until the 7th of July, when I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whilst you were in that room for that period of time, did you notice anyone from that room with injuries, after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. Meanwhile, while I was those - how many? - forty days or something. So during my stay there, they took two men to the administrative building and they stayed there for about two hours, were beaten there, and then they came back again to the room and they had injuries on their bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were these two men's names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: One of them was Mandzo. His last name was Mandzo. And the other one was Dzanko or Dzano, called Kalebic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Kalebic a nickname or a proper first name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the first name was, this Dzano or Dzanko?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It escapes me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that two men -- these two men were taken to the administrative building. Did you see them taken out to the administrative building or did you only discover that later?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I saw it through the window, through the window of our dormitory, because one could see the entrance into the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that "they took them to the administrative building." Who are you referring to? Who was "they"?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: That they were taken away by, a guard. A guard came to take them and took them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the guard wearing?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: That blue guard uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the guard?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I don't remember who it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that these two men came back two hours later to your room.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear or see or know what was happening to them during that two hours?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I don't know. All I remember is that when they returned to the room, they had severe injuries, but I cannot remember what had happened in the meantime while they were downstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've made a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in December 1998 about this incident. Have you had an opportunity to read that statement before coming to Court?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that statement, it states that when these two men were taken out, you heard screaming and moaning coming from the administration building. Is that correct? Did you hear screaming and moaning? Or is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When these two men came back to the administration -- came back to Room 16, did you notice anything about Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Mandzo had difficulty walking, and when he returned to the room, he lay down on the bed and showed us the soles of his feet, and that was a horrible sight, because they had taken his shoes off and beaten him on the soles. So his feet were swollen, there were cuts on his soles. And the other one, nicknamed Kalebic, had a cut on his face. I can't remember exactly whether it was here, whether it was on the right or left lower part of the cheek, but there was a cut. And he said that while they were downstairs, somebody had kicked him with a military boot, and he said that his skin had burst from that kick. And it was a terrible sight, and he bled a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he get any treatment for that cut?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No. No, there was no treatment. We had -- there was with us a physician, a surgeon, and he found an ordinary needle and some thread and managed to suture it a bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to Mandzo, you said that the soles of his feet were swollen and had a lot of cuts. Did you notice anything else about him in terms of injuries?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. He had bruises on his face and was swollen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Dzano or Dzanko stated that he was kicked, kicked in the face. Did he tell you who kicked him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say why he was beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No, he did not tell me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mandzo tell you who beat him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No. He said nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these injuries have any effect on Mandzo in terms of his ability to move about?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: True. He could not go to the canteen, to the kitchen for his meals for a couple of days, and it was only after a few days, when he recovered a little, that he could go to the kitchen, helped by others again, to eat something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this incident is related in Schedule B-18 and Schedule B-37.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you spent in Room 16, apart from these two, was there anyone else that you noticed that suffered from injuries?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. There was another one who was also taken to the administrative building, and he spent seven days there. His name was Zaim Cedic. And he also came back with injuries on his face and had also been beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first time that you knew that Zaim Cedic was beaten, is that when he arrived back in the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes, when he returned to the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him being taken away from the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I don't remember that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that he spent seven days in the administration building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: That is, I mean, what other prisoners said, that he was there for seven days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what injuries did you see on Mr. Cedic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: His face was all black and blue and swollen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he say who beat him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I did not talk about it with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this incident is referred to in B-11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were at the KP Dom, were detainees taken out and, to your knowledge, not seen alive again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. Whilst I was there, some 25 or 26 men were taken away, and they never returned, at least while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were you able to be sure of such a figure like that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, because we counted them when they took them away, and they were taking them away in threesomes or foursomes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see all of these 25 or 26 leave, or only some of them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: We saw all of them, because it usually happened in the evening hours, after dinner, a little before nightfall, so that we could see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how would you know when to look to see whether people were being taken away?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, somebody would see them through the window and let others know. Or the guard would come with the list and call out their names, so three or four men would go -- would follow the guard out, and then we would know what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would you look to see them taken out? From what position?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: We would stand by the windows in the dormitories and see them being taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About over how many days or how many times did you see these people taken away? You said they were in groups of about three or four. How often did you see these people be taken towards the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: It lasted for about two weeks, that is, it happened after dinner. Now, I cannot remember if it was every second night or every third night, but it was at that time in June, in early June, sometime in early June during that fortnight. It was at that time that those 25 or so men were taken out in groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you be more specific about who was, who was escorting them towards the administrative building? I think you said "guards" earlier.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: They were guards in blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of any of these guards?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember who exactly took whom when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any of the names of the detainees that were taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can think of all of the names that you saw taken out, and then we'll just discuss each one individually. Who were some of the people you saw were taken out and didn't return whilst you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I cannot recall all the names, but yes, I can, some of them. They were Halim Konjo; Nurko Nisic; Munib Veiz; then another Veiz, I don't know his first name; and Kemo Isanovic was another one in that group, in those groups; then Cedic; and then -- no, I can't remember it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you provide some further names in your statement that you've given the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. And there are other names, too, but I cannot remember them right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll mention the further names that you provided in your statement, and if you can tell me whether you remember of them being taken out. Kruno Marinovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Kruno Marinovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kemal Dzelilovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Kemal Dzelilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Husein Rikalo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Husein Rikalo, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a person with the surname Matovic, a Croat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Matovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Emir Prasto?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Emir Prasto, true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mehmed Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Pasalic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a person with the surname Selinovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Selinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether a Selinovic was taken out in the manner that you described just a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Like all the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, there is a problem with the answer to one of those. Perhaps you should ask him specifically whether all of the names that you read out to him were taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All of the names that I just read out, were they taken out in this period in the manner that you described?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see these people, the people that I've just mentioned, did you see them being taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anyone that I mentioned that you didn't see be taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people that you mentioned that were taken out, when I initially asked you to remember the names, did you see them be taken out, or did you hear that they were taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I saw them being taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you said that you saw Halim Konjo be taken out. After he was taken out, did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, when he entered the administrative building, a few minutes later, screams began and one could hear blows and cries for help, and I recognised his voice. I knew that it was he they were beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard screams. Did you hear him say anything, say any words?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I did not distinguish any words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Nurko Nisic, when you saw him taken out, did you hear anything after that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, when they took him in, blows began and screams, and I could hear some words, somebody say, "Nurko, die. What are you waiting for? Why don't you die?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did this beating appear to go on for? How long did you hear the sounds coming from the beating?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that exactly because we were all terrified because we were all stressed, in shock, so I can't tell you how long it went on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Kruno Marinovic, who was he? What job did he have before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was a radio and TV repairman, and he was also a correspondent of a Croatian newspaper, a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it is about 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Even from our view, the clock says 11.00 this time, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's a first, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We're grateful for the copy of that document filed by the Prosecution; in fact, my secretary found the copy that had been sent up and had been wrongly filed. We've read it. When would be a convenient time to deal with it, now or when the witness is finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Probably when the witness is finished, Your Honour, because I think Ms. Kuo would address that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, right. All right. Then we'll deal with it later, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we were previously discussing before the break the people that were taken out from their rooms and taken to the administration building and, to your knowledge, never been seen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, he mentioned Halim Konjo and Nurko Nisic. Halim Konjo is referred to at B-33 and C-13 of the schedules. Nurko Nisic is referred at C-19. And we've just spoken about a Kruno Marinovic, and he's referred to as C-17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that you saw a Kemo Dzelilovic being taken to the administration building. Did you know him before the war? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the name of the person you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kemo Dzelilovic.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how old was he and what work did he do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was an educator, a teacher, and he was about 35 or 40 years old at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's referred to as B-19 and C-7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a Husein Rikalo. Did you know him before you came to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was he and what work did he do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was an electrician, and at the time he was about 30 or 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: He's referred to at B-46, C-21. He mentioned, Your Honour, a Munib Veiz, and he's referred to at B-59 and C-28. He mentioned him earlier as being taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a Munib Veiz was taken out, and you also said another person with the surname Veiz was taken out. Do you know that person's first name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I can't remember his first name, but he was a policeman, worked as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he relate to Munib Veiz, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were relatives. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, a Zulfo Veiz is referred to at C-29. It may be that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you also mentioned that a Matovic, a Croat, was taken out towards the administrative building. Do you know the person's first name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I don't. I only know the last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know him from before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what work did he do and how old was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He worked as a medical technician and he was about 30 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, Matovic is referred to at B-39.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned you saw Emir Prasto [phoen] being taken out.

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Emir Frasto.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What work did he do and how old was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was -- he is probably my age, so he was probably 26 or 27 at the time, and he sold fruits and vegetables on the market, and for a while he also leased out -- he used to lease out a cafe called Derby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw Kemo Isanovic be taken out to the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was he, and what work did he do before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was a waiter before the war in a restaurant called Amadeus. He worked as a waiter in his relative's restaurant, and he was about 20 something, 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: This person is referred to at B-30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a Mehmed Pasalic was taken out towards the administration building. What work --

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What work did he do, and how old was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: He was about 35, 40, and as far as I can remember, he was a salesman, involved in sales prior to the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: He is referred to at B-43.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a Selinovic was taken out towards the administration building, but you didn't mention a first name. Do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what work did he do, and how old was he?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: I don't know what his profession was, and as far as his age at the time is concerned, like everybody else, about 35 or 40.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know him from before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Well, from passing. We were not really friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did he live?

utterances.speaker: FWS-3 [Name redacted]
utterances.text: Somewhere in town. I don't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
